drivers.variant_notes: Code update V4 (Spooky's Jetsons_Code.zip code update: Jetsons/JET_V004.PRG, Jetsons/PRP_V002.BIN and the SD card's folders), loaded as jetsons_004.zip. Every edition (IPDB 6577 Regular Edition; IPDB 6608 Special Edition) runs this code on the same board and playfield; PinMAME declares the set as a clone of the unreported pinHeck system set. PinMAME revisions before 97aa922b named it `jetsons`.

physical.notes: Firmware cabinet input 1 (U12 D0), published at 1 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk toggled it separately (released, then held again) instead of closing it. The factory chart prints 'COIN DOOR OPEN' in this cell. pinheck_brd_reset sets it at every reset because the door rests closed; the ROM printed DOOR CLOSE while it was 1 and dropped the text when the host released it, so 1 means the door is closed. Cabinet header pin 'door', wire gray/white.

Firmware cabinet input 2 (U12 D1), published at 2 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 2. Cabinet header pin 'launch', wire yellow.

Firmware cabinet input 3 (U12 D2), published at 3 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 112 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the right flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 112 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 112; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'R. flipper', wire gray/black.

Firmware cabinet input 4 (U12 D3), published at 4 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 114 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the left flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 114 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 114; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'L. flipper', wire gray/orange.

Firmware cabinet input 5 (U12 D4), published at 5 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it leaves the test; every walk used it to leave the test it ran. Cabinet header pin 'menu', wire gray/blue.

Firmware cabinet input 6 (U12 D5), published at 6 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it restarts the test; every walk opened the operator menu and started its test with it. Cabinet header pin 'enter', wire gray/green.

Firmware cabinet input 7 (U12 D6), published at 7 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 7. Cabinet header pin 'coin mech', wire gray/violet.

Firmware cabinet input 8 (U12 D7), published at 8 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 8. Cabinet header pin 'tilt', wire gray/yellow.

Factory switch 0, column 0, row 0. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure at factory switch 0 (column 0, row 0) of its 8x8 grid. pinHeck reads the matrix uncomplemented: board.c pulls a return line low for every closed contact in the strobed column and the driver has no invSw mask, so public 1 is the closed contact. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure while the host held public 1, so the contact rests open (normally_closed false), whatever its construction.

mechanisms.behavior: Balls rest in the trough on the trough opto 92 (Opto6) and the Ball Trough 1-3 contacts 52-54, with the jam opto 93 (Opto5) watching the exit. LOAD COIL (5) feeds one to the shooter lane; in the game-start run the ROM pulsed it about every 1.8 s for 20 s, because no ball ever reached the shooter switch.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough with optos

mechanisms.behavior: PLUNGER (6, the Ball Launch coil) fires the ball on the shooter lane switch 51; the cabinet Launch button is input 2.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and launcher

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 3 (host public 112), the ROM fires the RFLIP HIGH (4) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the RFLIP LOW (3) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 55 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 4 (host public 114), the ROM fires the LFLIP HIGH (7) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the LFLIP LOW (8) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 26 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: The Scoop coil (9) ejects a ball held on 21; the scoop opto 96 (Opto - 3) sees it enter.
mechanisms.label: Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: SAUCER (20, the Saucer Kick Out coil) ejects a ball held on 17 (Kickout Hole).
mechanisms.label: Kickout hole

mechanisms.behavior: BALL STOP (17, the chart's Up Post) between the orbits (11 right, 56 left) and the Elroy loop (16).
mechanisms.label: Orbit up-post

mechanisms.behavior: Servo 0 (57) drives the backbox topper, which IPDB lists only on the Special Edition, so the output is optional; the ROM's firmware has no Servo test, so its travel is not observed.
mechanisms.label: Orbitty topper (Special Edition)
